title: Access Tokens: Who am I? - Documentation - Lark Developer
snippet:
**The authentication method** is to tell Lark server "who is currently accessing this API" when the API is called. In other words, it allows Lark to know "who is accessing what tenant data now and in what capacity."
## Token categories
Access tokens available for the Lark API include the following three types:
- `tenant_access_token` **:** Tenant authorization token. With this token, the app uses its own account to perform corresponding actions, such as obtaining the information of a user from the contacts. The value of this token is prefixed with `t-`, for example: `t-24b5bf4e054bcef00b2af38a0b04f0af6d315b18`
- `app_access_token` **:** App authorization token. The open platform identifies the caller’s app, and the app can access information related to itself and not attributed to a specific company or user, such as obtaining the identity of the user currently logged into the app. The value of this token is prefixed with `a-` or `t-` , for example: `a-24b5bf4e054bcef00b2af38a0b04f0af6d315b18`
Note: In practical use, the `app_access_token` and `tenant_access_token` of the API response may be the same. This is due to the fact that `app_access_token` is used in fewer scenarios, and these two tokens are gradually unified on the Lark Open Platform.
- `user_access_token` **:** User authorization token. With this token, the app will perform actions on behalf of the user, such as creating a Docs or an Event through API. The value of this token is prefixed with `u-`, for example: `u-Lr1RT7S8fJUES03mT5FtWf`
You need to fill the access token into the request header parameter of the HTTP request when you call the API. Each Open API has an API that specifies the type of access tokens required and the way to obtain them.

For more information about Lark access token, refer to [API access token overview](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uMTNz4yM1MjLzUzM). Before the official start of development, developers are suggested to have a good understanding of Lark's access token mechanism.
> Note: The tokens should be placed in the HTTP request header and the value needs to be prefixed with``Bearer<space>`' , as shown below:

Use cURL sample code as follows:
```
curl --location --request GET`https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/contact/v3/departments/od-64242a18099d3a31acd24d8fce8d9f9c' \--header`Authorization: Bearer t-5888bcb7c421a695ca83c449caba5c0b12becfda' \--header`Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8'
```
- **About expiration mechanism of tokens*

title: Get user_access_token - Server API - Documentation - Lark Developer
snippet:
Last updated on 2025-06-09
OAuth token API for acquiring the `user_access_token` and `refresh_token`. The `user_access_token` serves as the user's access credential, which allows API calls to be made on behalf of the user. The `refresh_token` is used to obtain a new `user_access_token`.
- You need to obtain an authorization code before getting the `user_access_token`. For more details, see [Get Authorization Code](https://open.larksuite.com/document/common-capabilities/sso/api/obtain-oauth-code). Please note that the authorization code is valid for 5 minutes and can only be used once.
- During user authorization, the user must have [access to the application](https://open.larksuite.com/document/home/introduction-to-scope-and-authorization/availability). Otherwise, calling this API will return error code 20010.
- The obtained user_access_token has an expiration period. For instructions on how to refresh the `user_access_token`, see [Refresh user_access_token](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/authentication-management/access-token/refresh-user-access-token).
- If you need to obtain user information, see [Get User Information](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/authen-v1/user_info/get).
## Request
| Basic | |
|---|---|
| HTTP URL | https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/authen/v2/oauth/token |
| HTTP Method | POST |
| API Rate Limit | [1000 times/minute, 50 times/second](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uUzN04SN3QjL1cDN) |
| Supported Application Types | Custom apps Store apps |
| Permission Requirements | None |
| Field Permission Requirements | `refresh_token` and `refresh_token_expires_in` fields are only returned when the following permission is granted: Access authorized data offline |

### Request Body
| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| grant_type | string | Yes | Authorization type. **Fixed Value:** `authorization_code` |
| client_id | string | Yes | App ID of the application. How to obtain App ID and App Secret: 1. Log in to [Developer Consle](https://open.larksuite.com/app). 2. Enter the application details page, and click **Credentials & Basic Info** on the left navigation bar. 3. In the **Credentials** area, obtain and save the **App ID** and **App Secret**. **Example Value:** `cli_a5ca35a685b0x26e` |
| client_secret | string | Yes | App Secret of the application. How to obtain App ID and App Secret: 1. Log in to [Developer Consle](https://open.larksui

title: Obtain access tokens - Server API - Documentation - Lark Developer
snippet:
To improve API security, Lark uses an access token mechanism. When calling APIs, the access token authenticates the caller's identity and permissions. This informs Lark who is accessing app data and resources.
The access token is the key to accessing the Lark Open Platform, binding the caller identity, as well as all data access and API call permissions obtained by the app together, allowing the app to perform read and write operations on resources. It is recommended that developers have a thorough understanding of Lark's access token mechanism before starting formal development.
## Introduction to access tokens
The Lark Open Platform provides different types of access tokens for authenticating the calling party's identity. In the actual development process, you can choose the appropriate access token based on your business needs.
| Access Token Type | Requires User Authorization | Description |
|---|---|---|
| tenant_access_token | No | The credentials required to call the API as an app. The range of readable and writable data is determined by the app's own [data permission range](/document/home/introduction-to-scope-and-authorization/configure-app-data-permissions). The value of this type of credential is prefixed with `t-`, and the example value is: `t-24b5bf4e00b2af1234`. |
| user_access_token | is | The credentials required when calling the API as a user. The range of readable and writable data is determined by the user's data permission range. The value of this type of credential is prefixed with `u-`, and the example value is: `u-Lr1RT7S8fS03mT1234`. |
| app_access_token | No | The short-term token for app identity, the open platform identifies the caller's app identity based on the app_access_token. The value of this type of credential is prefixed with `a-` or `t-`, and the example value is: `a-24b5cef00b1234`. |
## How to choose different types of access tokens
APIs may support one or multiple types of access tokens. Different access tokens represent different resource access permissions. Therefore, different access tokens may provide different data information.
1. Confirm the supported access tokens for the API.
When calling the API, the access token needs to be filled in the HTTP request header. In the request header section of the Lark Open Platform API documentation, you can check the supported access token types for that API.
2. Choose the appropriate access token.

title: Obtain user_access_token - Documentation - Lark Developer
snippet:
Obtains the logged-in user's ID that corresponds to the login pre-authorization code.
## Request
| Facts | |
|---|---|
| HTTP URL | https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/authen/v1/access_token |
| HTTP Method | POST |
| Supported app types | Custom apps Store apps |
| Required scopes | None |
| Required field scopes | The response body of the API contains the following sensitive fields, and they will be returned only after corresponding scopes are added. If you do not need the fields, it is not recommended that you request the scopes. Obtain user's email information Only custom apps Obtain user ID Only custom apps Obtain user's mobile number Only custom apps Obtain user's employment information |
### Request header
| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Authorization | string | Yes | app_access_token **Value format**: "Bearer `access_token`" **Example value**: "Bearer a-7f1bcd13fc57d46bac21793a18e560" [Learn more about obtaining and using access_token.](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uMTNz4yM1MjLzUzM) |
| Content-Type | string | Yes | **Fixed value**: "application/json; charset=utf-8" |
### Request body
| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| grant_type | string | Yes | The auth type, whose value is "authorization_code" in this process **Example value**: "authorization_code" |
| code | string | Yes | From the [Request authentication](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/ukzN4UjL5cDO14SO3gTN) process. The user is automatically redirected to the redirect_uri with this parameter via a 302 redirect after login by scanning the QR code. **Example value**: "xMSldislSkdK" |
### Request body example
```
{    "grant_type": "authorization_code",    "code": "xMSldislSkdK"}
```

title: Calling APIs - Server API - Documentation - Lark Developer
snippet:
To facilitate developers in calling the API conveniently, Lark Open Platform provides Java SDK, Golang SDK, and NodeJS SDK. For detailed information about the SDKs, see [Server SDK](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uETO1YjLxkTN24SM5UjN). This article introduces the basic API calling methods.
## Prerequisites
- Before calling the server APIs, you need to complete the steps of creating an app, [applying for permissions](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uQjN3QjL0YzN04CN2cDN), [obtaining an access token](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uMTNz4yM1MjLzUzM), and [setting IP allowlist](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/ucTMxYjL3ETM24yNxEjN).
- When calling the server API, you need to include the access token in the request header `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`.
- When calling the server API, you need to use the HTTPS protocol and UTF-8 encoding.

You can use the [Send message](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/im-v1/message/create) interface to send messages to employees within an organization. Based on the interface documentation, prior to calling this interface, you need to obtain the `tenant_access_token`.
1. Refer to [Obtaining an access token](https://open.larksuite.com/document/ukTMukTMukTM/uMTNz4yM1MjLzUzM) to obtain the `tenant_access_token`.
The example request for obtaining the token is as follows. Please replace `app_id` and `app_secret` with the actual values.
```
curl -X POST 'https://open.larksuite.com/open-apis/auth/v3/tenant_access_token/internal/'-H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8'-d '{  "app_id": "<app_id>",  "app_secret": "<app_secret>"}'
```
2. Based on the request parameter description in the documentation, call the [Send message](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/im-v1/message/create) interface.
- Method 1: Initiate API call in the API explorer

### Querying user information
You can use the [Get user information](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/contact-v3/user/get) interface to query user information. Choose the appropriate access token based on the scope of user information you need.

title: Get authorization code - Server API - Documentation - Lark Developer
snippet:
This API is used to initiate user authorization. After the user consents to the authorization, the application will receive an authorization code, referred to as `code`. Please note that the authorization code is valid for 5 minutes and can only be used once.
## Notes
- This interface is actually an authorization page, suitable for the authorization scenario of web applications. When user authorization is required, the application should redirect the user to this authorization page. After the user clicks authorize on the authorization page (when the web application is opened in the Lark client, it can directly jump without confirmation), the browser will redirect to the address specified by `redirect_uri` and carry the `code` query parameter (i.e., authorization code).
- Developers can use the authorization code to obtain a `user_access_token` to call the OpenAPI (e.g. [Get User Information](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/authen-v1/user_info/get)). For detailed steps on obtaining a `user_access_token`, refer to [Get user_access_token](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/authentication-management/access-token/get-user-access-token).
- By using this endpoint along with [Get user_access_token](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/authentication-management/access-token/get-user-access-token) and [Get user information](https://open.larksuite.com/document/uAjLw4CM/ukTMukTMukTM/reference/authen-v1/user_info/get), the application can implement Lark OAuth login.
- For a complete implementation of the user authorization workflow, refer to the [Web App End User Athorization Guide](https://open.larksuite.com/document/common-capabilities/sso/web-application-end-user-consent/guide).
- Note that when opening the authorization page, you need to declare the user authorization scopes required by the application by appending the `scope` query parameter. For example, the scope key for obtaining basic contact information is `contact:contact.base:readonly`.
- The permissions granted by the user to the application accumulate over time, and the most recently generated `user_access_token` will include all the permissions the user has granted in the past.
